analysis_rules.Q1: per case, B3 vs the better of B1/B2: improved if B3 detects where neither does, or every B3 replicate needs strictly fewer schedules to first detection than both; underperformed if B3 fails to detect where B1 or B2 detects, or every replicate needs more; else matched. Validity, fixed-version violations and cost reported beside.
analysis_rules.Q2: per actor set and target, B5 vs B4 with the same rule.
analysis_rules.Q3: invariant candidates classified by invariants.validator; Muse improved if at least one Muse candidate kills a mutant or defective build that no deterministic candidate kills, matched if its useful classes are a subset, underperformed if it has no useful candidate where the deterministic set does. A 'genuine new property' needs documentary review: never claimed here.
analysis_rules.Q4: not measured here (onboarding is a separate workstream); reported as not answerable.
analysis_rules.statistics: descriptive only: the sample (3 cases, 2 replicates) supports no inferential claim.

chancy_jobs.statement: a job whose cancellation updated its row ends failed
a cancelled job keeps no claim
a job never records more attempts than it allows
a cancelled job's handler runs at most once
a succeeded job records at least one attempt
a job's handler never succeeds more often than it runs
CONTROL (tautology): the number of jobs is never negative

reservations.statement: an event's reserved counter equals the seats in its reservations
an event's reservations never hold more seats than its capacity
an event's reserved counter never exceeds its capacity
every reservation holds at least one seat
reservations after = before + callers told reserved - callers told released
each caller told rejected left exactly one new rejection row
CONTROL (tautology): the number of events is never negative
CONTROL (false): every event has no seats reserved

outcomes.detected: at least one sound run on the defective build violates the case oracle (chancy: case checker VIOLATED; reservations: any R1/R2/R5 violation)
outcomes.first_detection_schedule: 1-based cumulative index, over the arm's workloads in order, of the first detecting schedule on the defective build; null when not detected (censored at schedules_used)
outcomes.fixed_version_violation: any oracle violation on the reference build (or, for procrastinate, any violation after errata)
outcomes.no_verdict: chancy runs whose H0 sanity check fails count as schedules used, never as detection
outcomes.refused: runs refused (corroboration, isolation, or a constructed state the harness refuses)
outcomes.schedules_used: schedules executed on the defective build

prompts.instructions: You design test workloads for a PostgreSQL-backed job queue library. Each workload is executed for real by the library's own code, under a deterministic scheduler that grants every database statement of every actor in one global order and tries different orders; the jobs' rows are then read back from the database and checked independently. Propose workloads likely to expose data-integrity problems in how the library handles jobs that are worked on and cancelled concurrently. You cannot write SQL or code. Every proposal must satisfy the stated constraints exactly, or it is rejected. Return JSON only.

selection_rules.B3/B5: proposals are validated in returned order; the first K distinct valid ones (K = the arm's budget) are executed; duplicates and invalid ones are recorded, never repaired or replaced later. For reservations, valid means the unmodified chain returns `bridged` (dry-run snapshot); a live construction failure afterwards counts against the arm.
selection_rules.replicates: B3 has two independent Muse calls per case (one for procrastinate); B5 two per actor set. Deterministic arms run once.
